SoundBar 1.4
============

An audio visualiser for the MacBook Pro Touch Bar. It wakes up on its own when sound
starts playing or a microphone goes live, draws the spectrum across the whole strip, and
hands the Touch Bar back to BetterTouchTool (or to macOS) when the sound stops.

It runs as a background agent: no Dock icon, no window. Look for it in the menu bar.

Project home: https://github.com/ryoji-info/SoundBar


REQUIREMENTS
------------
  • A Touch Bar. Without one the app installs, runs, and has nothing to draw on. It talks
    to the strip through DFRFoundation directly, so there is no fallback window.
  • Apple Silicon. This build is arm64-only, which in practice means the 13-inch MacBook
    Pro (M1, 2020) or (M2, 2022) — the only Touch Bar Macs with Apple Silicon.
  • macOS 14.4 or later. A hard floor: SoundBar works out which apps are playing from
    per-process CoreAudio properties that do not exist before 14.4.


INSTALLING
----------
Double-click "Install SoundBar.command".

It copies the app to /Applications, registers it to start at login, and launches it. The
login agent has to name your home directory, which is why it is generated on your machine
rather than shipped ready-made.

You can instead drag SoundBar.app to the Applications folder. It will run when you open
it, but it will NOT come back after a restart until you run the installer — there is no
launch-at-login setting inside the app itself.


IF MACOS REFUSES TO OPEN IT
---------------------------
This build is signed ad-hoc, not with a paid Apple Developer ID, and it is not notarised.
If this disk image reached you over the web, AirDrop or email, macOS attached a quarantine
flag, and a quarantined ad-hoc-signed app is refused outright:

    "SoundBar is damaged and can't be opened. You should move it to the Trash."

That wording means "unsigned and quarantined", not "corrupt download". Do not trash it.
Clear the flag from the disk image before opening it:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ~/Downloads/SoundBar.dmg

or, if you already dragged the app across:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/SoundBar.app

Control-clicking and choosing Open used to work around this. On macOS 15 and later it does
not — that escape hatch was removed. System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security sometimes offers
an "Open Anyway" button after a blocked launch, but for the "damaged" case it usually does
not appear at all. The xattr command above is the reliable fix.


PERMISSIONS
-----------
  Screen & System Audio       REQUIRED. This is the one that matters. macOS files
  Recording                   system-audio capture under Screen Recording even though
                              SoundBar never reads the screen. Deny it and the Touch Bar
                              shows a flat line: macOS still creates the audio tap and
                              still calls back at full rate, but every sample arrives as
                              0.0. It fails silently, with no error.

  Microphone                  REQUIRED. Not only for the input meter — macOS checks this
                              when the system-audio tap is created too.

Nothing else is needed. Accessibility and Input Monitoring are NOT required.

Automation (controlling BetterTouchTool) is optional and cosmetic — it only lets SoundBar
name the Touch Bar group BTT restores afterwards.

Nothing is recorded, written to disk, or sent anywhere. Audio is read, turned into bar
heights, and thrown away.

If the visualiser draws a flat line while music plays, the Screen & System Audio Recording
grant is what to check first.


USING IT
--------
Touch Bar gestures (each can be switched off in the menu):

  one-finger tap     next colour palette
  two-finger tap     next pattern
  double tap         mute / unmute
  long press         toggle the visualiser off, or back on
  one-finger slide   volume

Menu bar:

  Pattern      11 of them — spectrum bars, fine bars, mirrored, mirrored fine, blocks,
               peaks, dot-matrix, waveform, and three VU meters (centred, inward, outward).
  Colour       9 built-in ramps: Rainbow (the default), Green, Spectrum, Ice, Ember,
               Meter, Mono, Sakura, Fable Computer.
  Behaviour    Fullscreen, what counts as a trigger, and Input Meter:
                 Off         output only
                 Auto        input only when nothing is playing
                 Mix         output and input together — the video-call case (default)
                 Input Only  microphone wins whenever it is live
  Turn On/Off  Another way back if a long press dismissed it.

More colours: SoundBar imports AVTouchBar-format colour sets. Drop them into
"~/Downloads/AVTouchBar Custom Colors" and they are picked up and cached automatically.
They are not bundled here — only the nine built-in ramps ship with the app.


WHERE THINGS LIVE
-----------------
  /Applications/SoundBar.app
  ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.ryoji.SoundBar.plist
  ~/Library/Logs/SoundBar/SoundBar.log
  ~/Library/Application Support/SoundBar/Colors      (imported palettes)
  Settings: defaults read com.ryoji.SoundBar

A few tunables have no menu item — notably barCount, frameRate, and usableWidth (how much
of the strip is actually visible on your machine, in points; the view is 1085 pt wide but
rather less than that is on screen). Set them with:

    defaults write com.ryoji.SoundBar <key> <value>

Then restart the agent so it picks them up:

    launchctl kickstart -k "gui/$(id -u)/com.ryoji.SoundBar"


UPDATING
--------
Run the installer again over the top; your settings and imported palettes are kept.

One wrinkle: because the signature is ad-hoc, macOS identifies the app by the exact hash
of its code, so any build with even a one-byte change is a different app as far as privacy
is concerned. After updating, if a permission looks enabled but nothing works, remove
SoundBar from the list in System Settings with "−" and add it back.


UNINSTALLING
------------
Double-click "Uninstall SoundBar.command". It stops the agent, removes the app and the
login agent, and offers to delete your settings.
